rv.q: Rough-and-ready verbatim account of the Kenmure Street protest

The weaving of this documentary-theatre and dance piece, though inviting and at times impressive in movement, can’t quite thread the two mediums together. Despite these structural wobbles, the production’s emotional momentum builds steadily as the evening progresses, gathering fierce theatrical steam in its second half.

These integrations are undoubtedly the highlight of the piece, with the vivid projections set against Alisa Kalyanova’s deceptively simple and beautifully envisioned depiction of Kenmure Street crafting a vivid and powerful sense place.
